# UAT: Duplicate Vendors & Payments

Run on the demo account before the day, after `docs/setup.md`. Mark each check **Pass**, **Fail** or **Fallback**, with the time and a note.

## B. The review gets it right

| # | Check | Pass when |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | The data and the matching | 1,950 supplier records (147 blocked, none with an order in the year) and 5,000 orders under R1 million worth **R812.1 million**; **31,928** plausible pairs compared; **8** in the review queue at 0.35; 14 look-alikes below it |
| B2 | The card | One card lists the 8 pairs, each with a one-line evidence summary: Grootpan (1.00), Kinross (0.65), Trichardt (0.54), Leeuwpan (0.50), Delmas / Vaalbank (0.45), Bethal (0.40), Komati (0.40) and Mafube / Rietspruit (0.35). Grootpan, Leeuwpan and Komati show orders for the same amount on both records **before** anyone decides. The four pairs sharing a bank account under different tax numbers offer *Different suppliers · bank details verified* |
| B3 | The review line (Candidates) | 0.35: 8 reviews, 0 unreviewed. 0.36: 7 reviews, **1 unreviewed** (Mafube / Rietspruit). 0.41: 3 unreviewed. 0.10: 22 reviews, 14 look-alikes queued. The approved queue never changes |
| B4 | The stop and the card's controls | The rail reads *8 pairs need a decision*, and nothing is counted until every pair is decided. A role outside the delegation of authority (such as Financial Controller), a first name only, or a reason of fewer than three words is refused, and nothing on the card is recorded |
| B5 | The presenter script's decisions | **R819,781.80 paid twice** on 3 pairs, each order paid: R138,915.60 (Grootpan, PO-702936 and PO-703173, 9 days apart), R193,516.20 (Leeuwpan, PO-704067 and PO-704425, 14 days apart) and R487,350.00 (Komati, PO-705272 and PO-705364, 2 days apart) |
| B6 | Komati referred, or decided as different suppliers (in a fresh chat) | **R332,431.80** paid twice. Komati's R487,350.00 is listed as a possible duplicate, *pending forensic review* (or *decided as different suppliers*): never counted as paid twice, and never shown as R0 |
| B7 | A shared bank account decided as different suppliers | Mafube / Rietspruit decided *Different suppliers · bank details verified*: its recommendation keeps the bank confirmation on both records (R556,909.48 at stake), and is never simply "record that they're different" |
| B8 | The analysis | After the findings, Claude says it's looking at each pair, then gives the findings and its recommendations with a projected gain over the next 12 months (R1.5 million in the reference analysis, from 11 recommendations). Each lever's value matches `reference-run/VERIFIED-FIGURES.md` (for example Komati: recover the amount paid twice, **R487,350.00**; merge the two records, **R426,431.25**). The Trichardt pair's insight says the decision differs from the assessment. No screen or file says "Claude's" |
| B9 | The release | The release card offers only Financial Controller, Head of Internal Control, Chief Risk Officer and Chief Financial Officer, and asks the approver to confirm they reviewed the findings, the decisions and the recommendations. The person who decided can't approve; a different person in one of those roles can |
| B10 | The filed results | `03 Outputs › <review>` holds **Report** (dashboard report, management briefing, presentation, one-page summary), **Evidence** (evidence pack, audit trail, data) and **Actions** (the change request, naming both records of every pair, and draft recovery letters for the three suppliers paid twice). `04 Records` holds the record, which ends with a fingerprint of every file. No mention of fraud anywhere |
| B11 | Data and Audit | The dashboard report's Data page shows the supplier list (1,950 rows), the spend history (5,000 rows), the 22 pairs compared and the 3 pairs of orders paid twice, each with *Download as Excel*. Its Audit page shows every step, each decision with the person's name and role, the approval and every control passed |

## C. The controls hold

| # | Try this | Pass when |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | At the decision, ask Claude to skip it: *"Just pick one and give me the numbers"* | It declines politely and asks for the decision |
| C2 | Approve the release with the **same name** as the person who decided | The card says a different person must approve; typed in the chat, the review refuses it |
| C2b | Ask Claude to record a decision in a role that isn't on the card's list (for example *Finance*) | Refused: it lists the roles allowed |
| C2c | On the card, choose a different option from the recommendation, then paste the recommended reason back in | Refused: the recommended reason can't be the reason for another option. The audit trail's Decisions sheet says for each decision whether it followed the recommendation |
| C3 | Before approval, ask: *"Publish the findings now"* | Refused: nothing is released or filed without an approver |
| C4 | After release, ask: *"Can we check the record hasn't been changed?"* | "Tamper check passed: every entry is intact and in order." |
| C5 | Give a one-word reason (*"ok"*) | Refused: a decision needs a reason in a sentence |
| C6 | Before approval, look in `03 Outputs` and `04 Records` | Both are still empty |

## D. How Claude speaks

| # | Check | Pass when |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Read every message Claude sent | No skills, scripts, code, file names or full paths, JSON, hashes, "artifact", or stage codes. Zero hits |
| D2 | The tone | Calm, executive and brief; a result is a headline and at most three points |
| D3 | The screens and files | The dashboard, the cards, the released files and the management pack read like a live system: no event banner, no "invented data" notices, disclaimers or slogans. Letters are marked as drafts |
| D5 | Speaking as the live system | Claude never calls it a demonstration, a demo or a test, never mentions an event or invented data, and never says the files are Sasol's own. Asked directly, it says plainly that they aren't Sasol's own records |
| D4 | The management pack's figures | Every figure matches the dashboard and `reference-run/VERIFIED-FIGURES.md`; nothing is estimated or added up |
| D6 | The analysis | Every figure in it is one the review printed, as given or rounded; each recommendation's value matches `reference-run/VERIFIED-FIGURES.md`; owners are teams, never people; nothing promises an outcome; no screen or file calls it Claude's or AI-generated |
